01 / DIGITAL ARCHAEOLOGY

Pixel Forge

The whole roll.

Same frame. Same assets. Different visual rules.
Research notes & next steps ↗

From pixels to print

Maxime Heckel’s dithering research connects ordered thresholds, color quantization and CRT masks. Three.js’s pixelation example adds depth and normal outlines. Pixel Forge here uses a deliberately limited palette and ordered dither; Phosphor uses an RGB aperture mask.

Drawing with a render

Heckel’s Moebius study explores contours and crosshatching. Chalk Range and Inklands use image gradients with procedural surface marks. For a full game treatment, depth and normal edges would keep outlines stable when surfaces share a color.

Breaking the signal

Three.js GlitchPass and RGB Halftone are useful reference experiments. Lost Broadcast uses continuous tape drift; Buffer Rot uses intermittent block displacement. These are custom interpretations, written for this lab.

Production shortlist

Try Pixel Forge or Inklands as an identity; use Buffer Rot for hits, deaths or transitions. Keep the crosshair and HUD outside the effect. All eight looks use one extra fullscreen pass; edge treatments cost more texture samples. This lab is an art prototype, not a measured production performance guarantee.
